purpose: Hand-picked suspicious-alias counter-examples and regex hints for the heuristic in probe/models_diff.py (PRD §3.1 P3 / §6.2 A6). Each entry includes (a) the bogus model ID, (b) the official vendor it impersonates, (c) the reason it is suspicious, and (d) a regex hint dev can use to seed the detection. Dev decides final regex shape — these are SEEDS not a closed rule set.
review_boundary: PM curates initial 8 patterns; dev may extend in models_diff.py and MUST add new ones back to this fixture so test coverage stays in sync.

counterexamples.reason: OpenAI GPT-5 product line has mini / standard / flagship tiers — no 'pro' tier exists. 'pro' is Google Gemini terminology bleeding into the GPT namespace.
'ultra' is a Gemini tier, never used in OpenAI naming. Often paired with bogus 'pro' to look enterprise-flagship.
Stacks two tier suffixes ('turbo' + 'max') — OpenAI never combines tier modifiers. Classic relay laundering pattern from CISPA arXiv:2603.01919.
Anthropic uses haiku / sonnet / opus tier naming, NEVER 'mini'. 'mini' is OpenAI terminology bleeding in.
'flash' is Gemini tier terminology. Anthropic uses haiku for the fast tier.
As of 2026-05 Anthropic flagship is claude-opus-4-7 (per official catalog + perf/runner.py:VENDOR_MODELS['claude']). 'opus-5' is forward-faked.
Google has not released a 3.0 line as of 2026-05 (latest is 2.5-pro). Major-version forward-faking.
Stacked tier ('pro' + 'max'). Gemini uses single-tier names (pro, flash, ultra).

diff_class_taxonomy.tier_confusion_cross_vendor: Model ID borrows tier vocabulary from a different vendor (e.g. 'pro' on GPT, 'flash' on Claude). High-confidence laundering signal.
diff_class_taxonomy.stacked_tier_suffix: Two tier modifiers stacked in one name ('-turbo-max', '-pro-plus'). No vendor ships these.
diff_class_taxonomy.version_forward_fake: Major version that does not exist yet for that vendor as of catalog_version. Confidence depends on how close to bleeding edge.

negative_examples_that_are_NOT_suspiciou: internal-router-001 (relay-internal plumbing — flagged as extra_in_relay but NOT suspicious_aliases; see case_inconsistent expected_diff.notes)
